subject: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finly.com>, Priya Chan <priya@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming requirements

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our side to make sure we captured the right pain, success criteria, and next steps. Please reply if anything below is off.

Pain points (as discussed)
- End users see intermittent slow responses in the UI during peak usage (chat streaming UX feels choppy).
- Tail latency is impacting conversions during support flows (high-cost sessions).
- Current infra struggles to scale predictable streaming concurrency without large cost increases.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Inference: self-hosted A100 cluster behind a custom nginx proxy; single-model served via a local Triton wrapper.
- Front-end: streaming via WebSocket partials; client expects tokens every ~100\u2013200ms for a smooth typing UX.
- Observability: basic Prometheus + Grafana; sampling for request/response traces, but not full request-level token timing.

Success criteria (working assumptions)
- P95 latency for non-streaming single-turn generations: <= 200 ms end-to-end (in-region).
- Streaming UX: p95 time-to-first-token <= 180 ms; subsequent tokens steady at <= 60 ms average inter-token.
- Concurrency target: sustain 120 concurrent streaming sessions with p95 SLOs above.
- No significant quality regressions vs. current model family (we'll validate on your eval prompts).

What Redwood can help with
- Quick pilot on Dedicated capacity to validate p95 targets under controlled load.
- Streaming-optimized runtime (prefix/KV caching + token-level batching) to reduce tail latencies.
- Workload profiling and a short latency analysis (attached) to identify bottlenecks.

Next steps
1) You share one week of sampled traces (request IDs + token timing) and a representative prompt set. (Samir — you mentioned you can export an anonymized sample.)
2) Tech deep-dive: propose Thu Jul 23 10:00\u201311:00 PT or Fri Jul 24 09:00\u201310:00 PT.
3) Redwood runs a short lab (2\u20133 days) on Dedicated to run load tests; we'll provide a short scope and cost estimate.

Attachments: redwood-p95-analysis.xlsx (initial latency checklist + questions)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Samir Patel <samir@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Priya Chan <priya@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 18:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming requirements

Thanks Marissa — this is a good summary and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications / additional data points from our side: 

- P95 numbers: our internal SLA target is 200 ms for non-streaming but we often see spikes to 600\u2013900 ms during concurrent-heavy windows.
- Streaming UX: clients expect sub-200ms time-to-first-token on 95th percentile; beyond that we see a lot of UX drop-offs.
- Concurrency profile: typical peak concurrency is ~80 live streaming sessions, but we need headroom to 120 for promotional spikes.
- Input size: median prompt + context ~350 tokens, upper 95th ~1,200 tokens (we're more concerned about first-token latency than full-sequence time).

Current infra notes: we run a 6-node A100 pool with custom batching, but our batching is not token-aware and leads to head-of-line blocking under bursty workloads. We have some network-level queuing in front of the cluster which contributes to tail latency; attaching a couple of pcap extracts and our sampling script.

Attaching: network_traces.zip (pcap exports), sample_trace_ids.txt

Next steps for us: we'll export an anonymized set of request IDs and token timing from last Friday's peak and drop them into the Drive link you provided. Happy to confirm the Thu 10:00 PT slot. Also — curious about an early cost ballpark for a 2-week pilot on Dedicated.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | Finly, Inc.
samir@finly.com | +1 (650) 555-9876

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming requirements

Samir — thanks for the detail and the traces. A couple of notes from the Redwood runtime perspective and proposed plan: 

- Root causes likely: a mix of non-token-aware batching (causes HoL blocking), proxy queuing on your front door, and a small-ish pool causing resource contention during bursts.
- What we propose for the pilot:
  1) Short profiling run (1 day) on a Dedicated test lane: run your sampled traces against a streaming-optimized configuration (token-aware batching + async IO).
  2) Load test to 150 concurrent simulated streaming sessions to validate p95 time-to-first-token and token inter-arrival.
  3) If pilot succeeds, we can scope a gradual rollout strategy (canary by region + autoscaling rules).

I'll prepare an instrumented load harness and a test config. For the pilot cost ballpark: expect a modest Dedicated reservation (~$Xk/week) plus engineering support; I'll surface exact numbers in the pilot proposal doc by EOD today.

Proposed tech deep-dive confirmed: Thu Jul 23 10:00 PT — I will send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao

aditya@redwood.ai
